> Whether `left` is below, equal to or above `right`, or
> STATIC_ENDPOINT_INCOMPARABLE when the answer cannot be given exactly.
> Two integers are compared in int128_t.  A comparison involving a real
> is done in double, which is exact for every real bound and for every
> integer of magnitude at most 2**53; a larger integer is refused, since
> rounding it could turn a strict inequality into an equality and so
> license the deletion of a check that was not redundant.

### Static_Interval_Contains

> RM 3.3(5) and RM 11.1: CONSTRAINT_ERROR is raised only when a value
> fails to satisfy a constraint.  When every value the inner interval
> admits already satisfies the outer one, no value can fail it and the
> check is dead - proved redundant, not suppressed, so the program's
> meaning is unchanged.  A null inner interval admits nothing and is
> contained in everything.

### Static_Interval_Excludes

```c
bool Static_Interval_Excludes (const Type_Bound *outer_low,
```

> Containment's dual: some value the inner interval admits provably lies
> outside the outer one, so the check cannot succeed.  The compiler may
> then replace the test by an unconditional raise - but only by a raise.
> RM 4.9 permits rejecting a *static expression* whose value is outside
> its subtype at compile time; the elaboration of a subtype indication
> is not that, and RM 11.1 requires the exception to be raised where the
> elaboration happens.
>

### Emit_Bound_Value_Typed

```c
uint32_t Emit_Bound_Value_Typed (Type_Bound *bound, LLVM_Rep *out_rep)
```

> A cache entry names the bound it evaluated by address, so an entry
> must not outlive the object that address belongs to.  Where the
> bound is a local of the emitter — an array aggregate's own bounds
> are — the frame that owns it marks the cache on the way in and
> releases back to that mark on the way out.  Without it a later frame
> that reuses the address is handed a register from a block that no
> longer dominates its use, and the module fails verification.

`ada83.c:33943`

### Emit_Bound_Value_Typed

```c
LLVM_Rep bound_rep = LLVM_Rep_Float (Width_Double);
```

> A bound of a real type is a real number, and truncating it to an
> integer here loses the bound entirely once its magnitude leaves
> the integer range -- which is where a floating point bound
> normally lives (RM 3.5.7).  The caller reads the representation
> back through OUT_REP and meets the bound in it.

`ada83.c:33970`

### Emit_Single_Bound

```c
uint32_t Emit_Single_Bound (Type_Bound *bound, LLVM_Rep target_rep)
```

> A bound in the representation the caller wants it in.
> 
> This function does NOT memoise, and must not: a Type_Bound reachable
> from a Type_Info is shared by every use of that type, while a
> register is meaningful only inside the function that emitted it.
> Caching there would hand one function's register to another.  A
> caller that needs a bound expression evaluated exactly once — RM
> 4.3.2 for an aggregate's choices, RM 3.6.1 for an index constraint —
> takes its own copy of the bound and memoises into that, which is
> what Aggregate_Bound_Cache is for.

`ada83.c:34201`

> RM 12.3: the actuals correspond to the formals one for one, and a

> RM 12.3.1: "a generic formal parameter of mode in of a given type is

> value of whatever character type is asked of it.

### Lookup_Path

```c
bool body_replaces_spec =
```

> RM 10.1: a library subprogram body submitted after a complete
> spec-only unit of the same name (an instantiation or a bodyless
> spec) replaces that unit; a spec that requires a body is instead
> completed by it.

`ada83.c:60400`

### Add_Include_Path

```c
const char *Add_Include_Path (const char *directory)
```

> Add DIRECTORY to the include path and return the entry that now holds
> it, or null if it was not added.  Paths are searched in the order
> they are added, so a directory already present keeps its position and
> its stored pointer: Lookup_Path_Ext recognises the runtime library by
> comparing that pointer against Rts_Include_Path, and a directory
> named twice must not end up with two identities.  The text is copied
> into the arena so callers need not keep their buffer alive.

`ada83.c:60431`

### Path_Directory

```c
bool Path_Directory (const char *path, char *out, size_t out_size)
```

> The directory part of PATH, or "." when PATH names a file with no
> directory at all.  False means the directory did not fit in OUT, and
> OUT is then untouched: a truncated directory names a different place,
> so the caller must treat it as a failure rather than search there.

`ada83.c:60457`

### Try_Load_From_ALI

```c
ALI_Cache_Entry *entry = ALI_Read (ali_path);
```

> An ALI file answers for its source only while the source has not
> changed under it: the checksum it recorded has to be the checksum of
> the text on disk now.  ALI_Read is memoized on the path, so the
> entry read here is the one the symbols are loaded from.

`ada83.c:60939`

### Load_Subunit_Context_Closure

```c
void Load_Subunit_Context_Closure (String_Slice subunit_dotted_name,
```

> RM 10.2: the context clauses of a subunit take effect before the
> elaboration of the ancestor library unit's body. Subunit bodies live
> in other modules, so their WITH'd units are loaded here (for their
> elaboration code) and ordered ahead of the ancestor's body, walking
> nested subunits through the library catalog.

`ada83.c:60986`

### Unit_Source_Filename

```c
char *Unit_Source_Filename (String_Slice unit_name, const char *extension)
```

> The filename a unit's source is reported under in diagnostics:
> the unit name with EXTENSION appended.  This is the name the parser
> is handed, not a name that is opened — the text has already been
> found by Lookup_Path, which knows the real file.

`ada83.c:61017`

### Adopt_Loaded_Body

```c
void Adopt_Loaded_Body (String_Slice unit_name, Syntax_Node *compilation_unit)
```

> Take responsibility for a body that has just been parsed and
> resolved: record that the unit's body is in, and queue the
> compilation unit for code generation.  A body already adopted is left
> alone — adopting it twice would generate it twice.

`ada83.c:61029`

### s

```c
Resolve_Context_Use_Clauses (cu->compilation_unit.context)
```

> RM 8.4: a use clause in a compilation unit's context clause is in
> effect throughout that unit, whichever kind of unit it is — so the
> use clauses are resolved before any of the forms below, not inside
> three of the four.

`ada83.c:61092`

### f

```c
if (not sm->type_address->base_type and
```

> One type, two Type_Infos.  'ADDRESS has to answer before
> SYSTEM is loaded at all, so it answers with the bootstrap
> one, and SYSTEM's declaration produces the other.  Binding
> the bootstrap type as a subtype of the declared one makes
> the pair one type for every question about type identity
> (RM 3.3: a subtype is of its base), which is what lets
> X'ADDRESS meet a subtype of SYSTEM.ADDRESS.

`ada83.c:61144`

### Load_Package_Spec

```c
Catalog_Entry *own_body = Library_Catalog_Find (name, CATALOG_UNIT_BODY);
```

> An obsolete body (older than the unit's current spec, or older
> than a spec it WITHs) is never loaded: RM 10.3 makes it an error
> only if it is still obsolete at bind time, by when a replacement
> compilation provides the body's code and elaboration.

`ada83.c:61302`

### Inputs_Are_Order_Sensitive

```c
bool Inputs_Are_Order_Sensitive (const char *const *inputs, int input_count)
```

> Two inputs on one command line are order sensitive when a later file
> names a unit an earlier file defines, or when both define the same
> unit: RM 10.3 requires a unit to be compiled after the units its
> context clause names, and the earlier file's ALI is what carries that
> information to the later one.  Order-sensitive inputs are compiled
> one at a time, in the order given; everything else may go in
> parallel.
> 
> Anything this cannot see — more names in a file than the scan holds —
> forces the sequential answer, because compiling in parallel when the
> answer should have been "sequential" is the failure that matters.

`ada83.c:62010`

### Compile_File

```c
Loaded_Body_Count               = 0;
```

> Everything one compilation accumulates, cleared.  A compilation,
> not a process: the driver's workers are forked from a parent that
> has already scanned the command line, and a compilation must start
> from the same state whether it is the first in its process or
> not.

`ada83.c:62106`

### Compile_File

```c
char library_directory[PATH_MAX];
```

> The library catalogue lives beside the IR: that is where this
> compilation writes its ALI file, so that is where the ALI files of
> units compiled earlier are.  Output to standard output writes no
> ALI file, so the current directory is all there is to read.

`ada83.c:62119`

### r

```c
for (int i = 0; i < unit_count; i++)
```

> Resolution has settled on one interpretation per expression
> (RM 8.7), so the legality rules that only a settled tree can decide
> run here — after every unit is resolved, before the error count
> decides whether anything is generated.

`ada83.c:62193`

### Compile_File

```c
bool main_program_compilation = false;
```

> A parameterless library procedure in this file is the main
> subprogram, and a program must be complete before it can run
> (RM 10.4).  A file holding only subunits is a fragment: its parent
> lives elsewhere, so it emits no entry point and no loaded bodies.

`ada83.c:62200`

### main

```c
{
```

> Include-path order, most specific first: the explicit -I paths
> (added above as they were seen), the runtime library shipped beside
> the executable, the directory of each input, then the current
> directory.  Every input's directory is searched, not just the
> first: which files a compilation can find must not depend on the
> order they were listed in.

`ada83.c:62451`

### const char *configured = getenv ("CC");

> Linking is delegated to a C compiler driver, which is what knows
> where the host's start files and C runtime are.  The candidates are
> tried in turn and only "command not found" moves on to the next: a
> driver that ran and failed has said something worth stopping for.

`ada83.c:62793`

### RM 2.1

- `ada83.c:7921` **Lexer_Skip_Whitespace_And_Comments** — RM 2.1/2.7: a comment holds graphic characters (and the horizontal tab); any other control character is an error.

### RM 2.2

# Part III — The short notes

One- and two-line remarks, under the function they sit in. A note marked
`»` sat at the end of a line of code rather than above it.

- `ada83.c:54445` Spin and park primitives.  Which pair a module gets depends on the host the compiler itself was built for, so the choice is made here and nowhere else.
- `ada83.c:54560` Rendezvous record allocation, caller release, absolute deadlines, and the bounded spin an acceptor does before it parks.

- `ada83.c:55054` Unlink a master record from its owner's list of owned masters (RM 9.4).

- `ada83.c:55140` Publish a master's done flag and wake the tasks waiting on the termination consensus (RM 9.4).

- `ada83.c:55333` The enclosing master with the given scope identity, for a task whose master is not the innermost one (RM 9.4).

### Lexer_Skip_Whitespace_And_Comments

- `ada83.c:7921` RM 2.1/2.7: a comment holds graphic characters (and the horizontal tab); any other control character is an error.  One diagnostic per comment is enough.

### Scan_Identifier

- `ada83.c:7949` RM 2.3: an underscore is embedded — never doubled, never last.  (Never first either, but a leading underscore cannot start an identifier: it is not Is_Alpha, so scanning never begins on one.)

### Scan_Number

- `ada83.c:8169` RM 2.4.1 against RM 2.2: the point of a real literal, and not the first character of ".." nor the selector of "1.ALL".
- `ada83.c:8214` RM 2.4.1: "An exponent for an integer literal must not have a minus sign" — a written sign is the error, even on a zero exponent.
- `ada83.c:8221` The token also carries the value in a machine integer where one fits, so that everything downstream of a literal small enough to be an ordinary INTEGER never has to reach for the big one.
- `ada83.c:8236` RM 2.4.1/2.4.2: the value is the numeral scaled by the base raised to the exponent, less one power of the base for each digit that fell after the point.
- `ada83.c:8249` A based real is held as an exact rational: no binary floating point representation is faithful to, say, 16#F.FF#E+2.

### Scan_Character_Literal

- `ada83.c:8269` RM 2.5: only a graphic character may stand between the quotes.

### Scan_String_Literal

- `ada83.c:8306` RM 2.2: a lexical element fits on one line, so an unclosed quote ends its literal at end of line rather than swallowing the rest of the file.
- `ada83.c:8315` RM 2.10: the % replacement form cannot carry a quotation mark — a string needing one must use the " form.

### Lexer_Next_Token

- `ada83.c:8398` Control bytes are spelled out: a raw one in a diagnostic turns the whole error stream into "binary" for text tools.

### Parser_Identifier

- `ada83.c:8851` A reserved word standing where an identifier is required was meant as a name (TYPE ACCESS IS ...): consume it and clear the panic so the construct's remaining syntax parses and later errors surface.

### Parse_Parameter_List

- `ada83.c:8924` RM 6.1: a default expression is only allowed in a parameter specification if the mode is IN.

### Parse_Pragma

- `ada83.c:9687` RM 2.8: parentheses on a pragma bracket a non-empty association list — PRAGMA P() is not a form of PRAGMA P.

### Parse_Case_Statement

- `ada83.c:9807` RM 2.8: a pragma may appear wherever an alternative may.

### Parse_Exception_Handlers

- `ada83.c:9873` RM 11.2: an exception part is the reserved word EXCEPTION followed by one or more exception handlers.  The caller has read the word, so an alternative must open here.

### Parse_Select_Statement

- `ada83.c:9994` RM 9.7.1: terminate_alternative ::= terminate; — it starts with no statement and carries no sequence of its own.

### Parse_Statement_Sequence

- `ada83.c:10141` Recover at the statement boundary: leaving panic mode here is what lets one bad statement yield one diagnostic instead of silencing every error after it.
- `ada83.c:10146` RM 5.1: a sequence of statements has at least one statement, and a pragma is not a statement.  The scan is over the whole list so that a sequence resumed after error recovery is judged once, as a whole.

### Parse_Subprogram_Designator

- `ada83.c:10563` RM 6.7 says which operator symbols a declaration may use, and the answer is the same wherever a designator is read — for a generic formal subprogram (RM 12.1.3) as for an ordinary one (RM 6.1).

### Parse_Generic_Type_Definition

- `ada83.c:10770` RM 7.4: private_type_definition ::= [limited] private.  LIMITED is the one form with two leading keywords, so it is read before the table.
- `ada83.c:10783` Every form but the array definition is recognised by its leading token alone; Parse_Array_Type reads ARRAY for itself.
- `ada83.c:10801` RM 12.1 names RM 3.6's array_type_definition itself, so the index list, its box and the component subtype are read by the parser that reads them for an array type declaration.

### Parse_Generic_Parameter_Declaration

- `ada83.c:10840` RM 7.4: the discriminant part belongs to the private forms.
- `ada83.c:10867` RM 12.1: the default is a name, or a box standing for whatever name is visible at the point of instantiation.

### Parse_Subprogram_Declaration

- `ada83.c:11047` RM 8.5: a renaming declaration stands where the body would.
- `ada83.c:11054` RM 6.3: subprogram_body ::= subprogram_specification is ...

### Parse_Compilation_Unit

- `ada83.c:11313` RM 10.1: a library unit is a subprogram, package, or generic — never a task unit, whose declaration needs an enclosing frame.

### Type_Admitted_Constraint_Forms

- `ada83.c:11599` RM 7.4.2: outside the defining package a private view offers its discriminants and nothing else, so no range or accuracy constraint may follow it even where the full type is scalar.
- `ada83.c:11611` RM 3.8.1 leaves an incomplete type's class unknown until its completion, and an unresolved name has no class at all, so neither composite form can be ruled out without inventing an error.
- `ada83.c:11617` RM 3.6.1, and RM 3.3.2's "must not already impose".

### Set_Fixed_Delta

- `ada83.c:12061` SMALL is the largest power of two that does not exceed DELTA, and the scale is that power's exponent.

### Real_Model_Of

- `ada83.c:12138` RM 3.5.7: D is the precision the floating accuracy definition asked for; a type that asked for none takes the precision of the format backing it.

### Type_Is_Boolean

- `ada83.c:12354` RM 3.5.2: BOOLEAN and CHARACTER are predefined enumeration types even though they carry their own kind tags, so the enumeration class holds all three and this is the class question, not the kind one.

### Symbol_Add

### main

- `ada83.c:62370` --bind is not an option but a mode: it consumes the whole command line and checks a library rather than compiling anything.
- `ada83.c:62427` --native takes one Ada source; any further inputs are .ll modules to be linked into the executable alongside it.
- `ada83.c:62487` The IR and its ALI are scaffolding for the backend; the artefact the user asked for is the executable.
- `ada83.c:62507` One forked worker per input, in batches sized to the machine. Inputs that must be compiled in a fixed order get a batch of one.
